memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'If you bring a grain offering of firstfruits to the LORD, offer crushed heads of new grain roasted in the fire. Put oil and incense on it; it is a grain offering.'" - Lev 2:14-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is the first grain of the season — the very earliest harvest, before the barns were full and before the farmer knew how the rest of the year would go.

That is what makes it costly. Giving from a completed harvest is easy arithmetic; you know what you have. Giving the first heads of grain is an act of trust. It says: I believe more is coming, because I believe in the God who sends the rain.

Notice how this offering was prepared — crushed and roasted in the fire. The tenderest, newest grain went through pressure and flame before it was presented.

There is a striking picture of Christ here, and the New Testament makes it explicit. Paul calls the risen Jesus the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep (1 Cor 15:20). He went through crushing and fire — Isaiah says it pleased the LORD to crush him (Isa 53:10) — and He rose as the first of a harvest still coming. His resurrection is God's guarantee that ours will follow.

So when you give God your firstfruits — your first hour of the day, the first portion of your income — you are not gambling. You are agreeing with a harvest that is already secured.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I give God my first and best, or what remains after everything else is settled?
2. How does Christ's resurrection as "firstfruits" change how I face the future?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You gave Your Son as the firstfruits and guaranteed the harvest to come. Help me to give You my first and best, trusting the God who provides the rest. Amen.
